subject: Request: FastPath latency commitment for Pegasus pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kline <sara.k@pegasuslabs.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: FastPath latency commitment for Pegasus pilot

Hi team,

Quick summary: Pegasus (contact Sara Kline) is asking for a timeboxed "FastPath" latency commitment for a Q3 pilot. They want a P95 response under 80ms for inference requests hitting their dedicated pool across us-west and us-east for the pilot (approx 150 qps steady, spikes to 400 qps for short windows).

Why this matters: Pegasus is moving forward with a paid integration but the procurement/legal teams are asking for an explicit low-latency commitment to include in the MSA. Sales needs an internal clearance on whether we can offer a conditional commitment (pilot only, capped duration, ops guardrails) and what product/ops asks we should include in the engagement checklist.

Attachments: pegasus_map_v2.pdf (product/usage map they provided).

Asks:
- David / Evelyn: what is the minimal product/ops path to make a sub-80ms P95 feasible for this workload? Dedicated pool + prewarmed cache?
- Grace: operational readiness — what runbook / escalation matrix will Pegasus require for a pilot-level commitment?
- Aditya: do you want a formal one-quarter pilot approval, or shall we route this through the standard SLA carveout process?

Proposed constraints to limit exposure:
- Pilot duration: 90 days
- Dedicated capacity: reserved pool with burst to shared capacity allowed only after agreed notice
- Measurables: daily P95 and error rate thresholds; automated rollback to standard model variant on regression

Can everyone reply with feasibility and preferred wording for the internal approval by EOD Tuesday so we can keep procurement on schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sara Kline <sara.k@pegasuslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FastPath latency commitment for Pegasus pilot

Thanks Marissa — looping in Evelyn for technical feasibility and Grace for ops. Sara, appreciate the extra context in the MAP. A couple of clarifying questions before we promise anything:

1) Are the 150 qps steady state numbers amortized across two regions (i.e., ~75 qps per region) or do they expect 150 qps per region?
2) What request types are most latency-sensitive (small prompt completions vs long-context generation)?
3) Are they open to a pilot with a capped committed RUs (so we can size reserved capacity appropriately)?

From a product/ops standpoint I want to understand the minimum guarantees we need to add to the pilot charter so it is operationally enforceable and reversible if we see regressions. Evelyn — can you flag any red lines (e.g., sub-80ms P95 cannot be sustained on model X without quantization or more GPUs)?

I think a conditional pilot approval (Aditya) with clear rollback metrics and an operational runbook is the right approach if the technical ask is achievable.

-David
David Kim
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sara Kline <sara.k@pegasuslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FastPath latency commitment for Pegasus pilot

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 08:03 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — looping in Evelyn for technical feasibility and Grace for ops.
> Evelyn — can you flag any red lines (e.g., sub-80ms P95 cannot be sustained on model X without quantization or more GPUs)?

Quick take: feasible with constraints. High-level notes below — attaching a quick snapshot from our internal bench (pegasus_latency_snapshot.csv).

Technical constraints / recommended configuration:
- Dedicated pool: required. We should size for 200 RUs to allow headroom (Pegasus steady 150 qps, buffer for bursts).
- Model variant: use the optimized quantized variant (q4_compat) for the pilot. Non-quantized variants push P95 above 120ms at this qps.
- KV cache: prewarm top prefixes (Pegasus provided MAP helps identify top-50 prefixes).
- Sequence length: ask customer to agree to 1024 token ceiling for the pilot; longer sequences introduce outliers.
- Monitoring: instrument per-token latency histograms, percentiles, and automated alerting on P95 > 80ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a compatible lower-latency model variant + immediate notification to both ops teams; during fallback we withdraw the "commitment" until metrics restore.

Operational asks for runbook (Grace to flesh out):
- On-call rotation and SLA contact (Pegasus primary + secondary emails)
- Escalation path: within 15 minutes for P95 breaches that persist >10 minutes
- Capacity ops: warm-start prescale thresholds, eviction/backfill policy for burst windows

Caveats: This is achievable for the limited pilot if Pegasus is willing to accept the quantized model variant and token ceiling. If they insist on non-quantized full context we should decline the low-latency commitment.

Next steps (technical):
- I will share the latency snapshot and a recommended capacity sizing within 24 hours.
- If approved, we need 5 business days to allocate and warm the dedicated pool before pilot start.

-Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kline <sara.k@pegasuslabs.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FastPath latency commitment for Pegasus pilot

Thanks everyone for the fast responses and the data. After reviewing Evelyn's notes and the attached snapshot I approve a timeboxed pilot-level FastPath commitment under the following conditions: 

1) Pilot duration strictly 90 days; measurable P95 target: <= 80ms (daily rolling)
2) Pegasus accepts the quantized model variant and 1024 token limit for the pilot
3) Dedicated reserved pool provisioned to Evelyn's sizing (200 RUs) and warmed 5 business days prior to start
4) Automated rollback to the lower-latency model variant if P95 > 80ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows; rollback pauses commitment until metrics are back in range
5) Customer signs the pilot addendum (pilot_commitment_signoff.docx) and accepts that the commitment is a pilot-level guarantee without an enterprise SLA credit clause

Grace: please produce the ops runbook and escalation matrix within 48 hours and include on-call assignments. David / Marissa: coordinate procurement for a capped commitment invoice that covers the reserved capacity for the pilot term. Evelyn: please confirm final sizing and share the warm-up plan.

Marissa — please send the pilot addendum to Sara and ask for a signed copy; if they push back on quantization or token cap, escalate to me.

Aditya Rao
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference
